t: You are at the site of St George Botolph Lane, a church that stood off Eastcheap in the ward of Billingsgate. The back of the church overlooked Pudding Lane, where the Great Fire of London started. A church is first recorded here in the twelfth century, and the fire of 1666 destroyed it. It was rebuilt by the office of Sir Christopher Wren, one of 51 City churches rebuilt that way after the fire. Wren is the architect also known for St Paul's Cathedral, and he is named as designer here. The church itself was demolished in 1904.
